_note: 4 shots, sparse. Mechanism: bad system. The delivery-notification loop where every party has technically done their job and the parcel is nowhere. Ends on the narrator defending the system that has defeated them.

premise.situation: A parcel is marked delivered but is not there, and the tracking says it was handed to a resident
premise.turn: The narrator becomes convinced there is a resident in the building nobody has met
premise.detail: the signature is a single wavy line

character_sheet: a man in his thirties, hoodie, standing in a shared hallway of a block of flats

beats.text: My parcel says delivered. It is not here.
The tracking says it was handed to a resident. Signed for and everything.
The signature is a single wavy line. That is the whole signature.
I have knocked on every door in this building. Nobody has it.
Which means there is a resident here that none of us have ever met.
I rang the company and they read the tracking back to me. Slowly.
So it has been delivered. Just not to anybody who lives here.
